title: Converge lint executors into a modular presubmit runner and add staged release smoke prober
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: Our presubmit pipeline mixes two strategies: large monolithic composite actions (fast to author but brittle and slow to iterate) and an ad-hoc set of shell scripts that are hard to reason about. This PR introduces a small, modular presubmit executor (Go) with a plugin-like runner model and a lightweight staged release smoke prober that runs short, deterministic checks before heavier release steps. Goals: reduce feedback latency for lint-only changes, centralize presubmit orchestration, provide a backwards-compatible shim for existing workflows, and gate release pipelines on a fast smoke layer to avoid long-running jobs when basic checks fail. Changes in this PR: 1) New presubmit runner: ci/presubmit/runner (Go-based) that loads task descriptors from YAML and executes work with per-task timeouts, concurrency limits and structured logging. 2) Split lint tasks into lightweight fast-lint shard and slow-style shard; the fast-lint shard runs by default on push and PR and returns results in <30s for common changes. 3) Introduced ci/release/smoke-prober which runs a set of deterministic probes against a staging environment: basic API health, sample streaming handshake, and an ephemeral inference smoke test with a costly token budget minimized to ~20 tokens. 4) Added metrics and tracing hooks (Prometheus labels + OpenTelemetry traces) for presubmit latency and release-smoke pass rate. 5) Compatibility shim: ci/actions/presubmit-composite-compat.yml invokes the new runner to preserve existing GitHub Actions interfaces for existing repo owners while allowing opt-in to the new declarative YAML. 6) Developer DX: added devcontainer quickpath and README with local-run instructions to iterate on presubmit tasks. Migration notes: Existing workflows keep working; repository owners can opt-in by replacing the small composite action call with a task descriptor in .ci/tasks/*.yaml. The compatibility shim will be removed after a deprecation period tracked in ENG-2345. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for runner task scheduling and timeout logic added (ci/presubmit/runner/***_test.go). - Integration smoke harness runs in CI on a dedicated ephemeral environment and is part of the merged checks. - Migration runbook and rollback steps included in the PR description and README. Rollout plan: staged rollout across teams: (1) enable fast-lint shard globally, (2) opt-in repos move to declarative tasks, (3) enable smoke-prober gating for release branches. Backout: revert to composite action entrypoint or re-enable legacy workflow flags. Checklist: - [x] Design review (ENG-2345) - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Devcontainer & local run docs - [x] Compatibility shim - [x] Metrics instrumentation - [x] Perf validation on canary repos Known limitations: the Go runner currently supports a subset of existing composite features (matrix expansion and secrets masking are implemented; artifact uploads are delegated to a small helper). Follow-ups: add cross-repo caching support and automatic task-pruning for tiny changes (ENG-2401).
commits: feat(presubmit): add modular Go-based presubmit runner with plugin task model
refactor(ci): split lint into fast and slow shards and wire fast-lint into runner
feat(release): add staged smoke-prober and small ephemeral inference check
docs: add devcontainer walkthrough and migration runbook
chore(ci): compatibility shim for existing composite actions
test: add unit and integration tests for scheduling and timeouts
small_snippet_examples:
// example task descriptor (ci/tasks/fast-lint.yaml):
name: fast-lint
steps:
  - run: go vet ./...
  - run: golangci-lint run --fast
  - timeout: 25s

# compatibility shim (ci/actions/presubmit-composite-compat.yml)
# preserves previous GH Actions inputs and invokes the new runner binary
review_comments: Ben Reynolds (review): Can the runner respect repo-level concurrency quotas? Please add a knob and default to 8 for monorepo-heavy repos.
Aisha Kumar (reply): Added a config key 'concurrency_quota' with a default of 8 and documented it in docs/presubmit-migration.md
Lina Cho (review): The smoke-prober test appears flaky in CI, sometimes timing out when the staging cluster is saturated. Can we reduce token budget and add retry semantics?
Aisha Kumar (reply): Reduced inference token budget to 20, added a deterministic retry backoff (2 attempts) and guard to skip prober if staging cluster reports >80% CPU load.
Marco Giannini (approval): Verified metrics emit and Prometheus labels look sane. Approving once the small flake is addressed.
CI Bot: integration-tests failed on first run (timeout on prober); re-run succeeded. All checks green.
release_notes: Introduce modular presubmit runner (Go) and staged release smoke-prober. Improves presubmit feedback latency via fast-lint shard, centralizes presubmit orchestration, and gates release pipelines with a lightweight smoke check. Backwards-compatible composite shim included. Migration documented in docs/presubmit-migration.md.
notes_for_ops: After merge: deploy presubmit-runner image to CI runner pool, flip feature flag 'presubmit_runner_v1' in ci-config for opt-in repos, monitor presubmit_latency and release_smoke_failure_rate dashboards. Coordinate removal of compatibility shim after 4 weeks and notifying teams via #infra-eng.
rollout_plan: 1) Enable fast-lint globally (Day 0). 2) Invite team maintainers to opt-in to declarative tasks over 2 weeks. 3) Enable smoke-prober gating for release/* branches on canary repos. 4) Remove compatibility shim after 4 weeks if adoption >75% (ENG-2345).
